A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MolLangBench and contain readable main text and complete Appendices A.1–A.22. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that scientific content matches; v4’s additional page results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations on molecular recognition, editing and generation tasks, with supplementary experiments, error analyses and repeated-run results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and the supplementary evaluations and variance analyses.

M1.justification: The task formulations, annotation and validation pipelines, and model prompting procedures are unchanged (Sections 2–4; Appendices A.1 and A.6). No algorithm or model component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UniChem-derived recognition, editing and generation coverage, complex-substructure tasks, molecular representations, and BBBP/BACE property-prediction tasks. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in corresponding main and supplementary experiments. This includes the general-purpose and vision-language models, plus ChemDFM, ChemLLM, Galactica, HIGHT and Llamole in Tables S6–S7.

E3.justification: Sampling procedures, sample counts, core/extended sets, zero-shot prompting, task exclusions and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The supplementary experiments retain their original settings and controls.

E4.justification: The prompt-sensitivity tests, structure-first prediction comparison, complexity and SELFIES analyses, OCR validation, and tokenization and failure cases are retained without revision (Appendices A.12–A.20).

E5.justification: Both report the same five-run o3 variance analysis and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Tables S9–S10, three-run property-prediction results in Table S8, and prompt-variation uncertainty in A.12.

E6.justification: All matched numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Tables 1–2 retain GPT-5’s 0.923/0.862 average recognition/localization accuracy, 0.855 core editing accuracy and 0.430 core generation accuracy.

T1.justification: The formal task mappings in Section 2 and pass@k definition in Appendix A.14 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, emphasis on precise and unambiguous outputs, and claims about current models’ limitations on fundamental molecule-language tasks.

C2.justification: The same tokenization and alignment hypotheses, structural-assembly explanations, and limitations concerning annotation cost and scalable data curation remain. No substantive interpretation or applicability qualification changes.

D1.justification: Code/data access information, model snapshots and hosting details in A.4, annotation instructions, OCR procedure and reproducibility statement are unchanged. The administrative additions provide no new experimental implementation details.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and complete bibliography are unchanged. The final ChemDFM reference moves onto a separate page in v4 but is already present in v3.

P1.justification: The correspondence footnote expands from Feng Luo’s email to Feiyang Cai and Feng Luo with both emails. Acknowledgments add Ling Liu’s NSF, IBM and CISCO support. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgment shifts the bibliography, leaving its final entry alone on v4 page 14 and moving the appendix one page later. All figures and tables retain their content, design and relative placement.

improvement.justification: v4 adds correspondence and funding information, accompanied by minor bibliography reflow. The benchmark design, empirical evidence, supplementary analyses, reproducibility documentation and scientific argument are otherwise identical. These administrative updates do not materially improve or diminish overall paper quality.
